data.title: Beyond malls and condos
data.description: Although the Chao Mae Thapthim Shrine remains standing, aggressive redevelopment has cleared out surrounding communities to make way for condominiums and shopping malls in the name of urban progress.

data.title: Indigenous Pgak'yau philosophy  on show during 'Life And Land'
data.description: The story about the Pgak'yau ethnic group and their approach to forest management is presented during "Life And Land", which kicks off today and runs until Aug 9 on the 3rd floor of Bangkok Art and Culture Centre, Pathumwan intersection.

data.title: Thai ancient history and art exhibition attracts visitors in Seoul
data.description: The Thai Culture Ministry expects at least 100,000 South Koreans to visit an exhibition of Thai history and art at the National Museum in Seoul.

data.title: Take 'The Road To The Golden Peninsula' at BACC
data.description: The rich history and multicultural heritage of southern Thailand are presented during "The Road To The Golden Peninsula", which will kick off tomorrow and run until Aug 9, on the Curved Wall, 5th floor of Bangkok Art and Culture Centre, Pathumwan intersection.

data.title: Reclaiming heritage
data.description: Busui Ajaw, a famous Akha artist, is aware that Akha culture is disappearing. She had been thinking about holding an exhibition to showcase and preserve her own culture for years, which led to her latest exhibition "The Preservation Of Fire" on display at Bangkok Kunsthalle.

data.title: Nadech Kugimiya  now on Netflix with  The Debt Collector
data.description: Superstar Nadech Kugimiya returns to small screens with The Debt Collector, a new action thriller film now streaming on Netflix.

data.title: Lucas Museum to display unseen 'Star Wars' pieces, curator says
data.description: SAN DIEGO - The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art -- founded by legendary "Star Wars" creator George Lucas and his wife -- will see previously undisplayed items from the hit sci-fi series after it opens later this year, its curator told AFP.

data.title: Reclaiming autonomy
data.description: Thipyaporn Khempila was born blind. Diagnosed with glaucoma, she experienced complete loss of vision in her left eye and partial loss in her right eye.

data.title: Sounds Of Wireless gives young musicians a stage to grow
data.description: Presented by the Royal Bangkok Symphony Music School, Sounds Of Wireless, a monthly series transforms the open lobby of 140 Wireless into a performance space where young musicians can rehearse, perform before live audiences, showcase their abilities and gain professional experience.

data.title: Rockin' in the Free World
data.description: Last year, World Beat went to the annual Boon Phra Wet Festival in Roi Et City in Isan. The three-day event celebrated one of the monthly merit-making ceremonies -- heet sip song -- with parades, huge dance performances (10,101 dancers on the streets), Buddhist sermons and nightly molam stages for both popular and traditional artists and ensembles.

data.title: Taiwan Documentary and Film Festival screening in Bangkok before Khon Kaen
data.description: Only two days remain for the eighth edition of the Taiwan Documentary and Film Festival, one of the most anticipated annual events for film lovers seeking distinctive stories and rarely screened works.

data.title: School for sleuths
data.description: Prime Video's three-part docuseries Murder 101, based on the hit US podcast of the same name, may look like another entry in the ever-growing true crime genre.

data.title: 'Power Of The Small' on show now at River City Bangkok
data.description: Art lovers and wellness enthusiasts are invited to discover a new perspective on well-being and celebrate everyday progress during "Power Of The Small", which is running on the 2nd floor of River City Bangkok, daily from 11am to 8pm until Aug 15.
